A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 24 pages of each version, including appendices A–F, equations, algorithms and figures, support a complete comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 report original GPT-2 training experiments, failure-isolation interventions and stabilized-training results. Appendix D also reports Llama-3.1-8B representation analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original GPT-2 experiments and stabilization results in Sections 3–4 and the Llama-3.1-8B analyses in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The conditional dynamic-maximum modification to safe softmax, its integration into Flash Attention and the unchanged backward pass remain identical in Section 4 and Algorithm 3.

E1.justification: OpenWebText language-model pretraining and the Llama-3.1-8B example analyses retain the same data and task coverage. No datasets, domains or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The Flash Attention comparisons and standard-attention/high-precision controls are unchanged. Spectral alignment is newly named as a monitoring signal, not evaluated as an additional comparator.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 replaces monitoring empirical indicators such as weight spectral norm with monitoring spectral alignment to identify failing configurations. This is a limited reported diagnostic-protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish reruns. Other experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The tiling, layer, head and precision interventions, rounding-error analyses, Llama case studies and multiple-maxima/loss analysis are retained. The revised monitoring description adds no analysis results or new ablation question.

E5.justification: Run and randomness reporting remain unchanged, including the recorded-batch replay procedure. Neither version adds uncertainty estimates, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported loss curves, spectral-norm values, rounding-error examples and appendix visualizations are unchanged. The figures retain identical numerical annotations and trends, with no added or removed result entries.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, the gradient-error derivations and the BF16 arithmetic reasoning remain unchanged. The new mention of spectral alignment introduces no mathematical definition or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same mechanistic explanation linking similar low-rank representations and biased rounding errors, and the same claim that a minimal Flash Attention modification restores stability.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning spectral-norm growth, attention sinks and stabilization techniques are unchanged. Section 5 and the appendices retain the same applicability qualifications and limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, precision settings, batch-replay instructions and code access remain unchanged. Spectral alignment is named and cited without additional implementation or reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: v4 adds Qiu et al., Spectral alignment for early detection of loss explosion in language models, and cites it in Section 3.2. The existing Gated Attention reference becomes Qiu et al., 2025b; the broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: One sentence in Section 3.2 is revised, citation year suffixes are updated and the arXiv version/date changes. The remaining prose, section order and appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Citation changes cause limited text reflow, and the added reference adjusts bibliography spacing on page 12. All 13 figures and three algorithm displays retain their content, formatting and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 adds attribution and revises the named failure-monitoring signal in Section 3.2, without defining that signal or adding supporting results. The mechanism analysis, stabilization algorithm, empirical evidence and limitations remain unchanged. These limited reporting and presentation edits leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
